purpose: Campaña de inicio; visualización publicitaria generada con IA, no foto exacta del artículo
prompt: Use case: ads-marketing. Create one premium photorealistic campaign BACKGROUND for Alambres Tandil, a real Argentine fencing-materials merchant. Ultra-wide 3:1 landscape composition. Product references attached: image 1 straight perforated concrete fence post, image 2 galvanized chain-link mesh roll, image 3 squared rough-sawn quebracho post. Preserve believable product geometry and authentic materials, use references only for physical product appearance. Art direction: sophisticated major-retailer commercial studio photography, NOT hardware-store clipart or a generic AI poster. Seamless saturated deep brand-red (#c90000) cyclorama and matching matte red floor, subtle real studio light falloff. LEFT 47% completely clear red negative space for HTML headline, no objects or decoration there. RIGHT half: meticulously arranged sculptural still-life of three actual full-height fence posts (one silver-gray concrete with drilled through-holes, one round natural eucalyptus pole, one reddish squared quebracho pole) leaning very slightly against one another, behind a generously sized dense galvanized diamond mesh roll resting on its side on the floor. Camera slightly low, restrained perspective, all products fit within upper/lower margins, real industrial scale and heavy mass. Small studio contact shadows and superb specular rim on galvanized wire, detailed end grain and rough concrete aggregate, focus-stacked clarity. Product cluster occupies x=55%-90%, maximum height 82%. Controlled softbox key from upper left and long grazing edge light, attractive but honest photographic textures, no oversaturation of wood. Entire scene shares the same red studio, no dividing seam, no white cutout. NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logo, NO watermark, NO badges, NO arcs, NO decorative geometric shapes, NO sparks, NO glowing effects. This is an art-directed premium retail photographic plate with beautiful material fidelity, no UI.
